-- # Oracle occurrence-count predicates — first authored pattern
-- 
-- One base pattern supplies six predicates. Catalogue release 1.0.0 remains frozen.
-- 
-- | Axis | Group by | Once | More than once |
-- |---|---|---|---|
-- | U01 | One selected column | U01.1 Uniqueness | U01.2 Non-uniqueness |
-- | U02 | Selected composite-key columns | U02.1 Composite uniqueness | U02.2 Composite non-uniqueness |
-- | U03 | Explicit record-comparison projection | U03.1 Record uniqueness | U03.2 Record duplication |
-- 
-- All six return original rows plus `profile_occurrence_count`. The two branches select count = 1 and count > 1. Every member of a repeated group is returned, including its first occurrence. There is no DISTINCT, representative-row selection or concatenation of key columns.
-- 
-- ## Customization
-- 
-- `{{schema_name}}`, `{{table_name}}` and `{{column_name}}` are identifier placeholders. `{{key_columns}}` and `{{comparison_columns}}` are comma-separated, alias-qualified column lists, such as `t.COL1, t.COL2`. The application supplies those names later. Quote individual identifiers when required by the database. These braces are substitution markers, not Oracle SQL syntax or bind variables.
-- 
-- Change `WHERE 1 = 1` inside the inner query to restrict the population, for example `WHERE t.ELECTION_ID = :election_id`. Both branches must use the same restriction. To exclude nulls from an investigation, add the appropriate non-null condition there; the supplied default deliberately includes null groups. For a composite key, decide explicitly whether all components must be non-null.
-- 
-- U03 compares the declared projection, not every displayed field automatically. A unique row identifier or audit timestamp should be included only if it belongs to the intended definition of record equality. Source rows are still returned in full so they can be inspected.
-- 
-- The derived alias `profile_occurrence_count` must not collide with a source column. If it does, change it both where calculated and where filtered. Unsupported partition types, including LOB content, need a separate variant; no implicit truncation or hashing is supplied.
-- 
-- ## Meaning and validation
-- 
-- The default includes null-key groups, in accordance with the approved catalogue. Composite keys are compared as tuples. Empty populations return no rows. No case/whitespace normalization or conversion is introduced; Oracle's datatype and collation semantics govern grouping.
-- 
-- The local fixture checks duplicates, null groups, partial-null tuples, distinct tuples that would collide under naive concatenation, changing comparison projections, filtering before counting, excluding nulls, singleton-null input, and empty input. The exact generated query structures were run using SQLite window functions as a portable logic check. **They have not been run against Oracle.** SQLite checks do not establish Oracle collation, datatype or optimizer behavior.
-- 
-- 
-- ## Primary references
-- 
-- - [Oracle 19c COUNT](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/COUNT.html): COUNT(*) counts all rows, including rows containing nulls.
-- - [Oracle 19c analytic functions](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/Analytic-Functions.html): multi-expression partitions and filtering analytic results in an outer query.
--

02.usage_notes:
-- Oracle SQL batch 02: population uniqueness (U04) and key candidates (U07).
-- Catalogue: frozen 1.0.0. Pattern: population_uniqueness.
-- Status: authored for human review; not executed against Oracle.
-- Local verification: all four queries passed 12 fixtures (48 checks) using
-- SQLite 3.53.1 for portable logic only: unique/duplicate populations, single
-- and repeated nulls, partial-null tuples, scalar vs composite grouping,
-- concatenation-collision examples, empty input and filtering before counting.
-- This does not test Oracle datatype, collation or execution-plan behavior.
-- Stable BEGIN/END markers identify queries for later code-based integration.
-- Run one statement at a time after replacing placeholders.
--
-- Bindings:
--   {{schema_name}} / {{table_name}}: individually quoted where required.
--   {{key_columns}}: alias-qualified column list, e.g. t.COL1
--                    or t.COL1, t.COL2. Use separate columns, not concatenation.
--   {{any_key_null_condition}}: one IS NULL test per selected key component,
--                    joined with OR: t.COL1 IS NULL OR t.COL2 IS NULL.
--                    Required only by U07. Must cover the same key as above.
-- These are application substitution markers, not Oracle bind variables.
--
-- Result: one summary row when the predicate holds; zero rows otherwise.
-- Empty input returns zero rows for both members (NO DATA, not a pass/fail).
-- For an unconditional diagnostic summary, remove the entire HAVING clause.
-- A diagnostic row with population_rows=0 and maximum_occurrences=NULL is empty.
-- duplicate_rows counts ALL rows belonging to repeated groups, not just extras.
-- null_key_rows counts rows with ANY null component, not null cells.
--
-- Scope/null rules:
--   Add cohort filters inside the subquery, before the analytic count.
--   Use identical filters/key columns for both members of a pair.
--   U04 defaults to including null groups, as in the occurrence-count batch.
--   U07 checks nulls as evidence of key failure: do not first discard null-key
--   rows when assessing the full intended population. Explicitly narrowing the
--   population only establishes a key candidate within that narrower scope.
--   Native datatype/collation grouping applies; no normalization is implicit.
--   Key columns must support Oracle PARTITION BY (no unchecked LOB truncation
--   or hashing). This does not assert future uniqueness or minimality of a key.
--
-- Reference syntax: Oracle Database 19c COUNT and Aggregate Functions:
-- https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/COUNT.html
-- https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/Aggregate-Functions.html

03.usage_notes:
-- Oracle SQL batch 03: distinct cardinality.
-- Catalogue: frozen 1.0.0. Pattern: distinct_cardinality.
-- Predicates: U05, U06, L02, L03, A02, A03 (12 member queries).
-- Authored for human review; Oracle execution has not been performed.
-- Verification: 52 local SQLite logic checks passed, covering null/excluded
-- inputs, empty/zero cardinality, repeated values, composite group/value keys,
-- boundary inclusion, and accepted-vs-admissible classification filters.
-- SQLite verification does not establish Oracle type/collation behavior.
-- Standalone work: integrate by BEGIN/END predicate ID markers at completion.
--
-- Common operation: select distinct values/tuples, then count them. Repeated
-- source rows do not increase a count. Tuple fields remain separate columns.
-- No concatenation, approximate count, implicit normalization or hashing.
--
-- Placeholders (replace before executing one SELECT at a time):
-- {{schema_name}}, {{table_name}}: source table/view identifier components.
-- {{value_columns}}: unqualified column names, e.g. COL1 or COL1, COL2.
-- {{values_nonnull_condition}}: matching IS NOT NULL tests joined with AND,
--     e.g. COL1 IS NOT NULL AND COL2 IS NOT NULL.
-- {{group_columns}}: unqualified determinant/subject column names, possibly
--     composite, e.g. ENTITY_ID or REGION_ID, ENTITY_ID.
-- {{groups_nonnull_condition}}: IS NOT NULL for each grouping component.
-- {{min_cardinality}}, {{max_cardinality}}: inclusive nonnegative integer
--     bounds, with minimum <= maximum. Required by U06 only.
-- {{accepted_assignment_condition}}: A02 filter selecting accepted assignments
--     in the intended scheme/time scope; 1 = 1 only for an already scoped view.
-- {{admissible_candidate_condition}}: A03 filter selecting admissible candidate
--     classes in a fixed scheme/scope that requires one class per subject.
--     Use 1 = 1 only when the input has already been prepared on that basis.
--
-- Column lists are unqualified because they appear at both query levels;
-- quote each identifier when required. If group and value lists share column
-- names, first give those operand roles distinct aliases in a source view or
-- edited subquery. Avoid collisions with the derived output count alias too.
-- All projected/grouped fields must support Oracle DISTINCT/GROUP BY.
--
-- Null policy: this batch's supplied eligibility conditions exclude nulls in
-- required value/subject components. Incomplete tuples are outside evaluation.
-- Use consistent eligibility in both members. U05 and L02 may be explicitly
-- adapted to count null as a category by relaxing the corresponding condition;
-- the findings then apply to that declared null policy. Do not interpret an
-- absent entity/class identifier as a related entity or classification.
--
-- Population queries U05/U06 return a summary row only when the predicate holds.
-- U05 returns neither member for zero eligible values. U06 deliberately counts
-- zero and selects the appropriate bounds branch, even on an empty source.
-- U06's count alone cannot distinguish an empty source from all values excluded.
--
-- Group queries L02/L03/A02/A03 return matching determinant/subject groups and
-- their distinct count, not individual source rows. Groups with zero eligible
-- values are absent from both branches. They need presence/coverage predicates.
-- L02 detects one vs multiple dependent tuples per determinant; a global X->Y
-- claim requires all intended groups, not merely one returned conforming group.
-- A02 counts accepted classes; A03 counts admissible competing candidates.
-- A02 multiplicity need not be an error. A03 applies only to single-class schemes.
-- Pin class identity/scheme and time scope in the source/filter as appropriate.
-- Source may be a prepared relationship/assignment/evidence view; these queries
-- do not infer joins or derive semantic acceptance from column names.
--
-- References: Oracle 19c COUNT and Aggregate Functions:
-- https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/COUNT.html
-- https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/Aggregate-Functions.html

04.usage_notes:
-- Oracle SQL batch 04: scalar equality and set membership.
-- Catalogue 1.0.0; P04, M01, P05, M02, M03, M04, A05 (15 predicates).
-- Standalone templates for later code-based integration. Oracle not executed.
-- Local verification: 52 SQLite logic checks passed (matching/nonmatching/null
-- sources, duplicate/null/empty sets, all three Boolean classes, assignment
-- scope, multiple assignments, and empty source). Oracle type/collation/empty-
-- string semantics were not executed in this portable check.
-- Run one marked query after replacing its placeholders.
--
-- Common identifiers: {{schema_name}}, {{table_name}}, {{column_name}}.
-- Quote each identifier component if required. Source alias is t.
-- {{default_value}}, {{selected_value}}: typed non-null Oracle literals or
-- bind expressions, e.g. :selected_value, 1, 'A', DATE '2025-04-28'.
-- Bind actual values with matching types; no implicit datatype conversion is
-- intended. A null selected/default parameter makes comparison indeterminate;
-- null testing belongs to P01. Default-valued does not prove default insertion.
--
-- Set placeholders: {{sentinel_set_query}}, {{selected_set_query}},
-- {{allowed_set_query}}, {{true_set_query}}, {{false_set_query}},
-- {{category_set_query}}. Each is a SELECT returning one comparable column
-- named member_value, with no trailing semicolon. Examples:
--   SELECT 'A' AS member_value FROM dual
--   UNION ALL SELECT 'B' AS member_value FROM dual
-- or:
--   SELECT CODE AS member_value FROM REF_SCHEMA.APPROVED_CODES
--   WHERE SCHEME_ID = :scheme_id
-- Explicit empty text set:
--   SELECT CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR2(100)) AS member_value FROM dual WHERE 1 = 0
-- Use the matching datatype for other domains. An unprovided set definition
-- is missing input, NOT a known empty set. Small literal sets may be edited
-- into IN lists for convenience if null/empty-set behavior is preserved.
--
-- EXISTS/NOT EXISTS tests membership. Null set rows cannot match a non-null
-- subject and duplicate set rows do not multiply output. A known empty set
-- has no members; all eligible subjects are outside it. All scalar queries
-- exclude null source values on BOTH sides. No sentinel/case/space rule is
-- silently added. Native Oracle equality and collation semantics apply.
-- Oracle ordinary empty strings are nulls, not independent category values.
--
-- M04 true/false sets MUST be disjoint under the actual comparison rules.
-- Null flags are excluded from all three branches. Unknown codes are the
-- non-null values in neither set. Overlapping sets are invalid configuration,
-- not an opportunity to guess precedence. NULL rows in either set are ignored.
--
-- A05 applies to subject rows, not individual assignment rows. Additional
-- bindings: {{assignment_schema}}, {{assignment_table}}, {{category_column}}.
-- {{subject_match_condition}}: matching subject/key fields using aliases a/t,
-- e.g. a.SUBJECT_ID = t.SUBJECT_ID (use AND for composite keys).
-- {{assignment_scope_condition}}: accepted assignments in the selected scheme
-- and time scope, using alias a; 1 = 1 only for an already scoped source.
-- {{classification_evaluable_condition}}: which subject rows have sufficiently
-- known classification to judge membership; include required non-null subject
-- keys. Example for a prepared complete population: t.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL.
-- Whether subjects with no assignments are known outside or unresolved is
-- decided by this explicit eligibility condition, consistently for both sides.
-- {{category_set_query}} specifies the selected category (normally singleton)
-- or its defined member codes. No hierarchy/descendant expansion is inferred.
-- Subjects can have several assignments: NOT EXISTS avoids misclassifying a
-- subject as outside A merely because another assignment is B. Assignment
-- duplicates do not duplicate subject results. The source preserves its rows.
--
-- Result: matching source/subject rows (t.*), with no added quality verdict.
-- Add cohort filters at the final WHERE level, identically for paired members.
--
-- References:
-- https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/IN-Condition.html
-- https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/Nulls.html

05.usage_notes:
-- Oracle batch 05: related-row existence. 18 predicates, one shared body.
-- User review/customization required; no Oracle execution has been performed.
-- Return matching subject-side rows (t.*), not joined combinations. Duplicate
-- related rows do not multiply subjects; duplicate subject rows are retained.
-- A predicate's positive/negative branches share identical subject eligibility,
-- key matching and related scope. An empty subject population returns neither.
--
-- Table slots expand to {{ROLE_schema}}.{{ROLE_table}}. Quote each identifier
-- component as needed. Alias t ALWAYS denotes the subject being classified;
-- alias r ALWAYS denotes the related row whose existence is tested.
--
-- Eligibility placeholders are SQL conditions in alias t, normally requiring
-- every relevant subject/key component to be non-null. Required non-null key
-- checks use AND, including composite keys. Do not treat a null foreign key as
-- an orphan unless the separate domain rule explicitly requires that meaning.
-- Match placeholders use alias r/t, for example r.ID = t.PARENT_ID, with AND
-- for composite keys. Use compatible native types; no implicit normalization.
-- Scope placeholders are explicit qualifying conditions in r (and t if needed).
-- 1 = 1 is appropriate only for a deliberately unrestricted/pre-scoped source.
-- All conditions must define a known, evaluable investigation; unavailable
-- sources, incomplete reference coverage or missing rule parameters are not
-- automatically evidence of absence. No live joins are inferred from names.
--
-- E03: t=subjects, r=events. Supply the required event kind and fixed observation
-- window in event_scope_condition, including time-boundary/timezone rules.
-- Example: r.EVENT_TYPE = :required_type AND r.EVENT_TIME >= :window_start
--          AND r.EVENT_TIME < :window_end. Missing events are classified only
-- relative to this explicit window and available observation coverage.
-- K01: t=source values/tuples, r=designated reference population.
-- K02: REVERSE direction: t=reference-side keys, r=source rows using those keys.
-- K03: t=children, r=parents. Exclude legitimate roots/null parent-key tuples
-- through child_parent_key_nonnull_condition. Reuse the declared parent scope.
-- K07: t=source values, r=crosswalk mappings. The mapping_scope_condition must
-- select actual available translations, not placeholder mapping rows with no
-- usable target. Uniqueness/ambiguity of mappings is a separate investigation.
-- A01: t=subjects, r=assignments. accepted_assignment_condition must select
-- accepted assignments with genuine class identity in the stated scheme/time
-- scope (e.g. r.CLASS_ID IS NOT NULL AND r.ACCEPTED = 1 AND r.SCHEME = :scheme).
-- An evaluable subject with zero such assignments is unclassified, not ambiguous.
-- G02: t=values/combinations identifying geography, r=chosen reference release.
-- The negative result means unknown TO THIS REFERENCE, not nonexistent globally.
-- G03: t=subjects, r=spatial mappings. usable_spatial_mapping_condition must
-- require a usable point/geometry representation under the chosen rules, not
-- merely any row with the matching subject. Coordinate domain/geometry validity
-- evidence can be pre-profiled or included here; existence alone does not prove it.
-- H03: t=EXPECTED domain members, r=observed facts. Start from the expected list
-- so absent fact rows can be detected. For one output per expected member, make
-- that expected input unique on the selected member key; otherwise repeats stay.
-- A known empty related population returns all eligible subjects on the negative
-- side. Unknown reference coverage is an investigation limitation to record.
--
-- Oracle reference:
-- https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/EXISTS-Condition.html

06.usage_notes:
-- Oracle batch 06: join-match multiplicity. Five predicates, one shared body.
-- Derived from Oracle-SQL-Library.json and Predicate-SQL-Mapping.json.
-- Customize placeholders and run one SELECT at a time. Oracle execution pending.
--
-- K04.1/.2/.3 classify eligible source rows by zero, one or multiple matches.
-- L05.1/.2 classify the same counts as <= or > the declared match allowance.
-- A match is a RECORD in the chosen reference population under the supplied
-- join condition and scope. COUNT(*) includes duplicate reference records and
-- records with null non-key fields. Distinct target identities are not counted.
-- This is the multiplicity of an inner join for each source row; zero matches
-- stays zero even though a LEFT JOIN would emit one null-extended output row.
--
-- Output: every selected source row, with profile_match_count appended.
-- Source duplicates remain separate. No source primary key or GROUP BY over
-- source columns is required, and related rows do not multiply the result.
-- profile_match_count must not already be a source column name; rename it in
-- both the inner SELECT and outer condition if needed. Alias p denotes the
-- profiled source rows, t the source, and r the reference.
--
-- source_eligibility_condition: the declared evaluable population in alias t.
-- For ordinary value/key matching require every source key component non-null,
-- e.g. t.KEY_A IS NOT NULL AND t.KEY_B IS NOT NULL, plus investigation filters.
-- Null-key rows are excluded, not silently labeled zero matches. A separately
-- declared null-safe join can use a broader eligible population consistently.
-- source_reference_match_condition: explicit condition in aliases t/r; e.g.
-- r.KEY_A = t.KEY_A AND r.KEY_B = t.KEY_B. Non-equality joins also work.
-- reference_scope_condition: accepted rows in r, with t allowed for correlated
-- scope such as an effective date. Use 1 = 1 only for a known unrestricted
-- population. A missing/unavailable reference is not a known empty population.
-- All branches must use identical eligibility, join and reference scope.
-- Match/scope expressions must be evaluable and stable for the investigation.
-- Use compatible datatypes; do not rely on implicit parsing or normalization.
--
-- match_allowance (L05 only): a finite, nonnegative integer Oracle NUMBER bind
-- or literal, e.g. replace every {{match_allowance}} with :maximum_matches.
-- Zero is valid. NULL, negative and fractional allowances produce neither
-- branch; treat this as invalid investigation input, not a passed test. Supply
-- a numeric value, not unvalidated text. NaN/infinity are outside this contract.
-- A single allowance applies to the investigation; no row-varying expression.
-- The explicit guards use TRUNC to exclude fractional allowances.
--
-- Empty source: no rows. Known empty reference: all eligible source rows have
-- count zero, so K04.1 and L05.1 (any valid allowance) select those rows.
-- COUNT(*) without GROUP BY returns one aggregate count, including zero. Do
-- not replace it with COUNT(nullable_column), COUNT(DISTINCT ...), or add a
-- GROUP BY/HAVING that could remove its zero-count row.
-- This is a customizable correctness template, not a performance guarantee;
-- inspect Oracle plans on representative data before large-scale execution.
--
-- Oracle references:
-- https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/COUNT.html
-- https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/Scalar-Subquery-Expressions.html

07.usage_notes:
-- Oracle batch 07: observed relationship cardinality. L01.1-L01.4.
-- Four predicates, one canonical body. Derived SQL; customize placeholders
-- and execute one SELECT at a time. Oracle execution has not been performed.
--
-- This is a POPULATION predicate: return one summary row when its class holds,
-- otherwise no row. It does not select individual entities or join records.
-- The result reports distinct pairs, participating left/right entity counts,
-- maximum distinct rights per left, and maximum distinct lefts per right.
--
-- Fixed orientation: 1:M means some LEFT entity has multiple RIGHT entities
-- and each participating right has exactly one left. M:1 is the reverse.
-- 1:1: both degree maxima = 1. M:M: both degree maxima > 1.
-- Each nonempty eligible population belongs to exactly one branch. Different
-- disconnected components can supply the two maxima: their combined population
-- is M:M even without one component exhibiting both branching directions.
--
-- entity_pair_query: a SELECT without a trailing semicolon, yielding observed
-- relationships and any columns needed for eligibility/scope filtering. It can
-- read a bridge table or join sources using the explicitly chosen relationship.
-- Do not manufacture a Cartesian product to represent unobserved pairs.
-- Choose the same snapshot, time window, orientation and entity identity for
-- all four branches. Missing observation coverage is not proof of absence.
--
-- left_entity_columns/right_entity_columns: nonempty comma-separated lists of
-- SIMPLE columns qualified with e, e.g. e.LEFT_ID or e.LEFT_KEY_A, e.LEFT_KEY_B.
-- Give every identity column a unique output name in entity_pair_query, with
-- disjoint left/right names. Those names must survive into profile_pairs.
-- Precompute expressions in entity_pair_query with explicit aliases. Do not
-- put AS aliases, concatenations, functions or extra descriptive attributes in
-- these column lists. Composite identities remain separate tuple components.
-- Example input: SELECT a.ID AS LEFT_ID, b.ID AS RIGHT_ID FROM ...
-- then left_entity_columns=e.LEFT_ID, right_entity_columns=e.RIGHT_ID.
--
-- entity_pair_eligibility_condition: explicit condition using e, requiring ALL
-- left and right identity components non-null, plus investigation scope, e.g.
-- e.LEFT_ID IS NOT NULL AND e.RIGHT_ID IS NOT NULL AND e.ACCEPTED = 1.
-- An outer-join row with a missing endpoint is not an observed relationship.
-- A null or partial-null identity is not silently treated as an extra entity.
-- DISTINCT uses only the identity tuples, so duplicate observations or join
-- records do not increase degree, even when their descriptive fields differ.
-- Use comparable Oracle scalar key components supported by DISTINCT/GROUP BY;
-- LOB/object identities need another representation. No lossy concatenation,
-- hashing, implicit conversion or normalization is introduced by this template.
--
-- Empty eligible edge population: all four branches return no row. No empty
-- relationship is declared 1:1. Entities with no observed edge are outside this
-- axis; coverage/mandatory participation require separate predicates.
-- This describes the chosen OBSERVATIONS, not a declared schema constraint or
-- proof that the relationship must retain this cardinality on future data.
-- Reference: https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/Aggregate-Functions.html

08.usage_notes:
-- Oracle batch 08: required relationship and expected-domain coverage.
-- L04.1/.2 and H04.1/.2; four predicates, one shared population-summary body.
-- Derived from the standalone canonical library. Replace placeholders and run
-- one SELECT at a time. Native Oracle execution remains pending.
--
-- Return ONE summary row if the selected coverage predicate holds, otherwise
-- no row. Output: profile_subject_row_count, profile_covered_row_count,
-- profile_missing_row_count. Each eligible subject contributes either one
-- covered row or one missing row. Duplicate related records never multiply it.
-- Full coverage means covered count = subject count; incomplete means less.
-- These are universal population tests built on the existence operation used
-- in batch 5, with a different output contract from its row-selection queries.
--
-- Empty-population policy: the frozen L04/H04 definitions say EVERY subject,
-- with no nonempty restriction. A KNOWN empty eligible/expected population
-- therefore selects the positive branch with all three counts zero. It does
-- not select the negative branch. This is vacuous coverage, not evidence that
-- any real subject exists. To require existence as well, combine with a separate
-- nonempty-population predicate. Do not silently change this shared definition.
--
-- L04: t is the subject population required to have a relation; r contains the
-- related records. subject_eligibility_condition defines who owes the relation,
-- e.g. t.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL AND t.REQUIRES_RELATION = 1.
-- subject_relation_match_condition explicitly joins t/r, e.g.

14.usage_notes:
-- # Policy, metadata and logical composition
-- 
-- Oracle 19c templates. No graph/ZIP access. No native Oracle execution. Run one rendered SELECT at a time after substitution. All queries return original source rows (plus diagnostic rule truth/counts where shown), except SC07 which returns one population summary when the predicate holds. Source fields must not collide with generated profile_* diagnostic aliases; rename conflicting fields in the supplied source query.
-- 
-- ## Declared business rules
-- 
-- B01 is the explicitly named rule extension point; B02 is an as-of lifecycle rule; B03 is the declared eligibility rule. `subject_query` supplies the evidence with alias t. Conditions are SQL conditions, not stored boolean guesses. Their evaluability conditions must establish required inputs and knowledge. Example B01: `t.AMOUNT <= t.LIMIT_AMOUNT` with both inputs nonnull. Example B02: `t.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' AND t.START_AT <= :as_of AND (t.END_AT IS NULL OR :as_of < t.END_AT)` when NULL end explicitly means open-ended, with known status and start/as-of inputs. Bind one fixed as-of instant and consistent timezones. B03 can use `t.SCORE >= :required_score AND t.REQUIRED_TRAINING = 'Y'`; null knowledge stays unevaluable. Unknown conditions produce NULL truth and neither branch. Conditions must be safe to evaluate independently of WHERE predicate order; prepared safe parsed inputs where necessary.
-- 
-- B06 requires an available marker interpretation. Example `t.DELETED_FLAG = 'Y'` with known marker scope `t.DELETED_FLAG IN ('Y','N')`. Unexpected/null codes are not presumed non-deleted; an explicitly meaningful null encoding can be declared. Does not detect physically removed records.
-- 
-- ## Imported metadata
-- 
-- SC01 starts from expected objects and EXISTS/NOT EXISTS in a complete supplied inventory. SC04 starts from required constraints. Match full owner/schema/object identity and object kind, not just names; constraints can match normalized requirement descriptors including ordered column tuples and referenced objects/check definitions where applicable. Completeness of the imported inventory is mandatory for absence claims; missing privileges or an incomplete extract is not evidence of absence. Source/reference aliases t/r match the existing related-existence template. Scope is the same on both branches. SC04 only tests declaration, not enabled/validated behavior.
-- 
-- SC02/SC03 use an unambiguously aligned actual/expected metadata input query. Supply nonnull normalized complete type descriptors (e.g. NUMBER(10,2), VARCHAR2(20 CHAR)) for actual_type_expression/expected_type_expression. If comparing only DATA_TYPE, explicitly label the narrower base-type investigation. Use source metadata, not inference from row values. Nullability expressions similarly normalize known declarations, e.g. t.NULLABLE and t.EXPECTED_NULLABLE using Y/N. Unknown descriptors are excluded. Oracle scalar equality/collation applies; normalize descriptors deliberately in the supplied query, preserving byte/character semantics.
-- 
-- SC05/SC06 reuse scalar equality: schema_name/table_name point to prepared known-constraint metadata; column_name is the normalized enablement/validation column. SC05 accepts only ENABLED/DISABLED; SC06 only VALIDATED/NOT VALIDATED. Other and null values select neither member. Status alone does not prove historic data correctness, constraint type, or enforcement at other times.
-- 
-- SC07 compares the sets of selected metadata tuples using MINUS in both directions. old_metadata_query/new_metadata_query expose the same uniquely named columns; metadata_columns is a nonempty unqualified column list including object identity and every selected property. No lossy concatenation. Use comparable Oracle scalar fields, excluding raw LONG/LOB fields unless safely represented by an appropriate full comparison strategy. Set semantics intentionally ignore duplicate identical inventory rows. Null properties compare as equal in set operations, but unavailability of an entire required property makes snapshot_scope_known_condition false. Align owner filters, relevant extraction times and completeness; include identity so additions/removals are counted. Both known empty sets are unchanged. Output old-only and new-only tuple counts, not changed-object counts.
-- 
-- ## Logical components
-- 
-- LC01-LC03: subject_query yields subject_id and source fields. subject_id is a stable nonnull identity on a common population; composite identities can use a collision-free surrogate mapping, not concatenation/hashing. Repeated source rows remain repeated output rows. component_definition_query supplies the selected component_id set; duplicates are deduplicated, and NULL component IDs are outside the selected set and are ignored. component_result_query supplies subject_id,component_id,truth_value, with truth_value using a numeric datatype (for example Oracle NUMBER), where 1=true,0=false,NULL=unknown. Normalize text encodings safely before supplying this query; the template does not parse arbitrary text truth values. Select a fixed rule set, scope and evaluation version. Exactly one evaluation per required component and subject is required: missing evaluations, duplicate evaluations (even agreeing), null or invalid truth codes exclude the subject from both branches. Unselected component results are ignored. Input components must describe the same subject population and snapshot. Empty selected component sets use mathematical identities: ALL=true, ANY=false, EXACTLY_ONE=false. Counts make that fact visible; it does not prove a substantive rule was checked.
-- 
-- LC04 uses the rule classifier: conditional_scope_condition establishes common evidence scope, antecedent_condition is P, consequent_condition is Q. Only true P enters; false/unknown P and unknown Q select neither branch. An implication with false P is not treated as satisfied because the frozen definition excludes it.
-- 
-- ## References
-- 
-- - https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/CASE-Expressions.html
-- - https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/The-UNION-ALL-INTERSECT-MINUS-Operators.html
-- - https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/refrn/ALL_CONSTRAINTS.html

    FROM {{schema_name}}.{{table_name}} t

    GROUP BY {{observed_category}}
), profile_domain AS (
    SELECT {{baseline_category}} AS profile_category,
           CASE WHEN {{baseline_share}} BETWEEN 0 AND 1
                          AND {{baseline_share}} IS NOT NAN AND {{baseline_share}} IS NOT INFINITE
                THEN CAST({{baseline_share}} AS NUMBER) END AS profile_baseline_share,
           CASE WHEN {{share_allowance}} BETWEEN 0 AND 1
                          AND {{share_allowance}} IS NOT NAN AND {{share_allowance}} IS NOT INFINITE
                THEN CAST({{share_allowance}} AS NUMBER) END AS profile_allowance
    FROM {{baseline_schema}}.{{baseline_table}} b
    WHERE ({{baseline_scope_condition}})
), profile_totals AS (
    SELECT (SELECT SUM(profile_count) FROM profile_observed) AS profile_population_count,
           (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM profile_domain) AS profile_domain_count,
           (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM profile_domain
            WHERE profile_category IS NULL OR profile_baseline_share IS NULL
               OR profile_baseline_share < 0 OR profile_baseline_share > 1
               OR profile_allowance IS NULL OR profile_allowance < 0 OR profile_allowance > 1
               OR profile_baseline_share IS NAN OR profile_allowance IS NAN) AS profile_invalid_count,
           (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT profile_category FROM profile_domain GROUP BY profile_category HAVING COUNT(*) > 1) d) AS profile_duplicate_count,
           (SELECT SUM(profile_baseline_share) FROM profile_domain) AS profile_baseline_total,
           (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM profile_observed o WHERE NOT EXISTS
                (SELECT 1 FROM profile_domain b WHERE b.profile_category = o.profile_category)) AS profile_undeclared_count
    FROM DUAL
), profile_representation AS (
    SELECT b.profile_category, b.profile_baseline_share,
           GREATEST(0, b.profile_baseline_share - b.profile_allowance) AS profile_lower_share,
           LEAST(1, b.profile_baseline_share + b.profile_allowance) AS profile_upper_share,
           1.0 * COALESCE(o.profile_count, 0) / NULLIF(t.profile_population_count, 0) AS profile_observed_share,
           t.*
    FROM profile_domain b LEFT JOIN profile_observed o ON o.profile_category = b.profile_category
    CROSS JOIN profile_totals t
    WHERE t.profile_population_count >= {{minimum_sample_size}} AND {{minimum_sample_size}} >= 1
      AND t.profile_domain_count > 0 AND t.profile_invalid_count = 0 AND t.profile_duplicate_count = 0
      AND t.profile_undeclared_count = 0
      AND {{baseline_sum_tolerance}} BETWEEN 0 AND 1
      AND ABS(t.profile_baseline_total - 1) <= {{baseline_sum_tolerance}}
)
